topic: The conference report explains little
claim: The Senate had replaced the entire text of the House bill with its own; in conference, the House agreed with a substitute for both versions. Conferees met July 19 and 24, 2002. The joint explanatory statement records this but gives no section-by-section explanation.
quote: The Managers on the part of the House and the Senate met on July 19 and July 24, 2002 (the House chairing), and reconciled the differences between the House bill and the Senate amendment.

locator.section: Joint Explanatory Statement of the Committee of Conference

notes: Because the conference report gives no reasons for individual sections, the Senate report (S. Rept. 107-205) and floor debate are the best library sources for congressional purpose. Provisions added on the Senate floor (e.g. Sec. 402's ban, Title VIII) have no committee report explanation.

topic: SEC 704 study: where fraud happens
claim: Studying 515 enforcement actions (227 investigations) from July 1997 to July 2002, the SEC found improper revenue recognition was the most common problem (126 matters), and 157 matters involved charges against at least one senior manager.
quote: The Study found that 157 of the 227 enforcement matters involved charges against at least one senior manager.
notes: Same summary: the SEC charged 18 audit firms and 89 individual auditors in the period (PDF p. 7 [p. 3]). The study was required by SOX Sec. 704. Enron is not counted in these statistics.
